headline: Kazakhstan's Saiga Antelope Makes Historic Comeback
meta_description: Kazakhstan's saiga antelope population has surged to 4.6 million, a remarkable recovery from just 25,000 in the 1990s.
summary_short: A species brought to the brink of extinction has staged a remarkable comeback. Kazakhstan's saiga population now exceeds 4.6 million.
body:
Kazakhstan's saiga antelope population has surged past 4.6 million, marking one of conservation's most dramatic turnarounds. The species that once hovered near extinction has reclaimed its place on the steppes.

The scale of the recovery becomes clear when looking back: saiga numbers plummeted to around 25,000 in the 1990s, a catastrophic collapse that seemed irreversible. Today's population represents not just survival, but genuine restoration of an entire species to ecological abundance.

This breakthrough demonstrates what sustained conservation effort can achieve. The saiga's journey from the brink back to thriving populations offers a rare beacon of hope for other endangered wildlife worldwide.
quick_facts: Saiga population now exceeds 4.6 million in Kazakhstan
Species recovered from just 25,000 individuals in the 1990s
Represents a historic conservation comeback for endangered wildlife
